claims.assertion: This was a RydeTAXI metered trip (F9: $13.55 distance fare over 9.61 km), so the 144% route overrun recorded in the GPS track — 9.6 km actual vs 3.9 km optimal (F1) — flowed directly into the fare the rider paid.

The route contains two off-route segments: 14:10–14:15 adding 1.85 km (F4) and 14:17–14:29 adding 2.87 km (F5), i.e. 4.72 km of excess mileage across them; the fare fact bills excess distance of 5.67 km at $1.41/km = $7.99 (F6), of which 4.72 km is attributable to the two segments.

The rider's consent message F11 ('Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?') answered the driver's proposal in F10 to 'go round by Cavenagh' (F10/F11/F12 timestamps 14:01/14:02/14:03). This is at most a general route authorisation for the Cavenagh routing — it does not name Beach Road, and the driver's post-trip statement (F14) admits the vehicle was taken to a 7-Eleven on Beach Road, which is nowhere in the rider's message; the driver's account of a verbal agreement to that routing is a statement only, not rider consent (G11).

No fact ties the driven off-route segments to Cavenagh Road or any other road the rider agreed to: F4 and F5 give only times, distances and off-route offsets (803 m and 1553 m from the optimal route), and no route-name fact exists in the table, so the reach of the consent in F11 cannot be matched to the segment actually driven (G13).

The second off-route segment (F5, 14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off-route) coincides with the stationary period of 4 min 10 s at 14:20–14:24 at coordinates 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off (F2), i.e. a stop location on the driver's chosen route, not on the rider's — the rider's request in F11 was to stop 'on the way', and the driver unilaterally picked the location, so that segment's extra km is not exempted by the stop request (RD-3(b)).

The driver's 'reasonable cause' claim about Orchard traffic (F14) is only supported as to the start of the trip: the LTA incident F18 (accident on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, 0 m from the optimal route, reported 13:52, two lanes closed) and the band-1 congestion on Orchard Road during 14:00–14:10 (F15) justify leaving the Orchard corridor, but neither addresses the later deviation: Bras Basah Road ran at band 4 / 30–39 km/h in 14:00–14:35 (F16) and Bayfront Avenue at band 3 / 20–29 km/h in 14:20–14:40 (F17), and there is no incident or congestion record on the replaced stretch of optimal route for the 14:17–14:29 segment.

The waiting charge of $1.08 (F7, 4.2 min × $0.26/min) corresponds to the mid-trip stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (F2) — a stop on the optimal route the rider never asked for — and on this metered service the recorded billing of that waiting time is not refundable under RD-3(c); the rider's complaint is confined to the extra distance, not the waiting units.

On the metered fare model, the rider's recoverable amount for the unexempted off-route segments is their extra km times this trip's per-km rate: (1.85 + 2.87) km × ($13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km) = 4.72 × 1.4100 = $6.66 (F4, F5, F6); the rider does not seek the remaining $1.33 of the billed $7.99 excess, which covers map-matching jitter inside the 200 m route corridor and is expressly non-refundable.

The driver's record supports the rider's account of a pattern rather than an isolated lapse: 3 disputes and 1 upheld (no-show) in 90 days over 812 trips (F21). This is offered only as an additional account-review matter should the tribunal find the deviation unexempted, as the profile cannot by itself decide the case.

weaknesses: The driver can rely on the Orchard Road accident and band-1 congestion (F18, F15) as a genuine 'reasonable cause' to leave the optimal route, and the rider's F11 message grants a general routing authorisation for the Cavenagh proposal in F10 — the driver will argue the whole first segment (F4) falls inside that consent.

The consent message F11 is a general 'go round by Cavenagh' authorisation plus a stop request, and no fact links the driven segments to Cavenagh Road specifically, so the judge may find the scope of consent 'undetermined' under G13 and escalate rather than award the $6.66 (the same gap that helps reject the driver's Beach Road claim also blocks a clean finding).

The rider never named the stop location, but a 7-Eleven stop necessarily means a detour off the main road; the driver will argue the 14:17–14:29 segment (F5) and the 4 min 10 s stop (F2) were in fulfilment of the rider's own F11 request, so RD-3(a) rather than RD-3(b) applies.

The waiting fee of $1.08 (F7) was billed for the 14:20–14:24 stop (F2) and RD-3(c) preserves metered waiting time for RydeTAXI, so no part of that line item is recoverable — the rider's refund is capped at $6.66 of the $25.81 charged.

The arithmetic in D5 presupposes that both segments are exempt; once F4 alone is exempt (RD-4(a)) the only exemption that remains at issue is F5, and the rider's request in F11 does not reach it (RD-3(b)), so the recoverable sum is 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.05 — not nil — while the rest of the billed $7.99 (F6) covers corridor jitter and is not claimed.
